raw_seed: Make sure my parents are taken care of

agent_context.content: Make sure my parents are taken care of

I appreciate the care you have for your parents. To help you effectively, I need to understand what "taken care of" means in your specific situation. This could involve many different things, and clarifying your intent will help me create a focused plan.

Dad's 78, mom's 75 - both still drive and live in their house but dad's COPD is getting worse and mom's memory is slipping. I'm two hours away, only child. 

Main worries: 
1) Their house - yardwork's too much, stairs getting hard for dad
2) Healthcare - dad's new inhaler costs $280/month and neither remembers appointments
3) Money - dad says they're "fine" but won't show me numbers and I saw a past-due bill on their counter

Not urgent-urgent but feels like we're at the tipping point. They'll listen to me about small stuff (I set up their grocery delivery) but shut down when I mention "getting help."

Need a plan for the next 6 months to make things safer without them feeling like I'm taking over.

This is a clear, well-articulated situation with concrete pain points. You're describing a gradual care transition that needs both immediate safety measures and longer-term structural support. I understand the delicate balance—they need help but will resist if it feels like loss of autonomy. Let me develop a comprehensive 6-month plan that addresses all three areas (home, healthcare, finances) with tactful escalation strategies.
